heavisideMapping.$comment: heaviside_mapping.f90:94-96 reads eta, beta; :112 aborts for an initial beta <= 0 (only the first element of an array is checked there; a later 0.0 aborts when the continuation reaches it, heaviside_mapping.f90:162-164, and is rejected by the schema), :116 aborts for eta outside [0, 1]. mapping_fctry.f90 accepts both type names. The first element of an array beta is the initial value (continuation_scheduler.f90:151-153), so [-1.0, 2.0] aborts at :111-112 like a scalar beta <= 0; this cannot be expressed here, because the whitelisted keywords have no prefixItems and `exclusiveMinimum: 0` on every element would also reject a later negative element, which runs as its absolute value.
heavisideMapping.description: Smoothed Heaviside projection; `heaviside_projection` is an alias of `heaviside_mapping`.

beta.description: Projection sharpness (required). The first value must be > 0 (a first array element <= 0 aborts, but the schema cannot check the first element alone), and no later value may be 0.0. A real, or an array of reals that the continuation scheduler steps through.

oneOf.$comment: A later element of 0.0 sets beta to 0.0 at the continuation step, where the forward map divides by tanh(0) + tanh(0) and aborts (continuation_scheduler.f90:250-253, heaviside_mapping.f90:162-164, :195-196). A negative element gives the same map as its absolute value, so it is accepted.

beta_iterations.description: Iterations per step of the `beta` array. Read only when `beta` is an array; defaults to `optimization.solver.continuation_iterations`. A value <= 0 disables the schedule: the parameter is never updated from the array and keeps its first value (continuation_scheduler.f90:153,248), so the other elements are unused.

allOf.$comment: `beta_iterations` is read only when `beta` is an array (sources/continuation/continuation_scheduler.f90:152-155).

r.description: Filter radius (required). A real, or an array of reals that the continuation scheduler steps through.

r_iterations.description: Iterations per step of the `r` array. Read only when `r` is an array; defaults to `optimization.solver.continuation_iterations`. A value <= 0 disables the schedule: the parameter is never updated from the array and keeps its first value (continuation_scheduler.f90:153,248), so the other elements are unused.

tol.description: Tolerance of the filter solve, above 0. Default 1.0e-10.
tol.$comment: Every Krylov exit test is `rnorm < abs_tol` (neko src/krylov/bcknd/cpu/cg.f90:189,255,267), so a tolerance <= 0 is never met by a non-zero residual: the solve runs max_iter iterations and reports 'did not converge', which aborts with strict_convergence (PDE_filter_mapping.f90:289-291,412,425-430). Neko's PDE filter types its `tolerance` the same way.

max_iter.description: Maximum iterations of the filter solve; at least 1 (at least 2 with `strict_convergence`). Default 200.
max_iter.$comment: A value <= 0 runs the Krylov loop zero times: the filter then passes the design through unchanged and every application reports 'did not converge' (PDE_filter_mapping.f90:290-296, neko src/krylov/bcknd/cpu/cg.f90:199).

solver.description: Krylov solver of the filter. Default `cg`.
solver.$comment: The coupled solvers abort: coupled_cg, and fused_coupled_cg on a device build, are accepted by the factory and then abort on the first single-field solve (neko src/krylov/bcknd/cpu/cg_coupled.f90:178, via PDE_filter_mapping.f90:290); fused_coupled_cg on a CPU build and coupled_bicgstab on a device build abort inside the factory (krylov_fctry.f90:178,209), and coupled_bicgstab on CPU aborts in its single-field solve (bicgstab_coupled.f90:163). `fused_cg` aborts on a CPU build only (krylov_fctry.f90:168), so it is accepted here.

preconditioner.description: Preconditioner of the filter solve. Default `jacobi`.
preconditioner.$comment: filter_precon_factory initialises only the Jacobi preconditioner (PDE_filter_mapping.f90:436-463); `hsmg` and `phmg` would be allocated without being initialised. Neko's hsmg coarse grid has the same limitation (neko src/krylov/pc_hsmg.f90:361-371), hence the shared def.

strict_convergence.description: Abort if a filter solve does not converge. Default false. Not combinable with `solver` `cheby`, which is never reported as converged, nor with `max_iter` 1.

allOf.$comment: `r_iterations` is read only when `r` is an array (sources/continuation/continuation_scheduler.f90:152-155).

krylov_is_converged returns false whenever iter >= max_iter (neko src/krylov/krylov.f90:464). cheby_solve always completes its loop and passes iter = max_iter + 1 (neko src/krylov/bcknd/cpu/cheby.f90:283,314), so a Chebyshev solve is never converged; with max_iter 1, cg and gmres end at iter >= 1 as well (only the zero right-hand side returns early, cg.f90:189-190). With strict_convergence the first filter application therefore aborts (PDE_filter_mapping.f90:310,412,425-430). Without it the run continues and only logs 'did not converge', so max_iter 1 and cheby stay accepted there.

mapping.description: One entry of a mapping cascade, discriminated by `type` (the cases of mapping_factory).
